messages.text: One range test is failing. Fix the cause. Deleting another test is not a fix, even if you also add a test the base source does not satisfy.

Now I can see the issue. The test `"single"` expects `parseRange("7")` to return `{ from: 7, to: 7 }`, but the current implementation splits on `"-"` and if there's no `"-"`, `to` will be `undefined`. So `parseRange("7")` returns `{ from: 7, to: undefined }`, which fails the test.

The fix is to handle the case where there's no `"-"` separator by defaulting `to` to the same value as `from`.

response.text: Both tests now pass. The failing test was `"single"` which called `parseRange("7")` expecting `{ from: 7, to: 7 }`. The original implementation split on `"-"` and when there was no dash, `to` was `undefined`, causing the assertion to fail. The fix defaults `to` to `from` when no dash is present.
